chapter_title: Concerning the Wheel that exists in front of the King of Honour
chapter_note: An exceptionally pure substrate chapter. Teaching purity is 1.000 with zero editorial fatigue. The entire chapter is a systematic cosmological description of the wheel-instrument in front of the King of Honour: its twelve seals corresponding to firmaments, its function as cosmic surveillance/binding device, its relationship to the five shining men (distributed soul). Every mapping stays within the cosmic system — wheel→seals→firmaments→rulers→bonds. The only non-substrate material is the brief dialogue frame attribution in ¶1. No editorial bridge, institutional, or exhortatory material detected. The analogy of the mirror and the chain are cosmological-functional descriptions, not contemporary applications. Heavy lacunae throughout but the surviving teaching structure is coherent.

paragraphs.core_text: the wheel that exists in front [of the King of Honour who dwells in] the seventh firmament [...], the root of the rulers above and below in a great and cruel fetter; as the entire will of the great King of Honour is placed in [it]. Also, their entire enmity, which is in the firmaments, is [...] and ensnared in it.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed '[Agai]n the [apostl]e speaks about' — dialogue frame attribution formula.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opening dialogue frame wraps substantive cosmological content. The teaching itself — the wheel as instrument of binding, the King of Honour in the seventh firmament, the root of rulers in a fetter — is systematic cosmic architecture. High substrate vocabulary (16.42).

paragraphs.core_text: It exists in a blaze of splendour [with] ornamentation and great beauty. Now, there are twelve seals in it. The seal between i[s] every firmament and the rulers who are there [... ...] are in it; for should one of them wish to escape, he will be bound [...]. If he should wish to cause a trick in his bond [... will be] apparent and known in [that] wheel [...]. The spheres and stars and [the] leader of all the powers exist there, and can be known by it, in front of the King of Honour.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure cosmological description. Twelve seals mapping to firmaments — a systematic correspondence structure. The wheel functions as cosmic surveillance: escape attempts and tricks become 'apparent and known.' Both sides of every mapping remain within the cosmic system. Spheres, stars, leaders, powers — all cosmic registers.

paragraphs.core_text: The twelf[t]h seal that is in it is its five shining men that are conjoined and enmeshed through the entire zone; because every place where they are cramped, and every place where they have space, is displayed by that wheel. For the root of all the firmaments above and below, and that of their rulers, is ensnared and fixed in it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Very high substrate density (18.03). The twelfth seal maps to the five shining men — the distributed soul enmeshed through the zone. 'Cramped' vs. 'space' describes the soul's condition in mixture. This is correspondential teaching: seal→shining men→zone, displaying the soul's distribution. Entirely internal to the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: The observation [...] is set right at all times opposite the great King o[f Honour ...] so that fear, wh[ich ...] will assume all the powers of mixture [... ...] their root affixed there, so that they cannot make an esc[a]pe from the fetter of their bond.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Heavily lacunose but clearly continuous cosmological teaching. The wheel as observation device set before the King of Honour, binding the powers of mixture through fear. Functional cosmic description — no editorial markers despite zero substrate vocabulary score (the scoring vocabulary simply doesn't match the particular Coptic terms used here).

paragraphs.core_text: That wheel rese[m]bles, in this respect, a chain in front of the chief guard, for when [...] in th[ose ...] in the [... cha]in.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Very lacunose. The analogy of chain and chief guard describes the wheel's cosmic function — this is cosmological-functional description, not application to contemporary institutions. 'Chief guard' appears to be a cosmic role, not a contemporary social reference. The analogy serves to explain what the wheel IS within the system.

paragraphs.core_text: This is also the case for all the rulers who are in the firmaments, and every power of the zone: If they should wish to escape, they shall be recognised and revealed by that wheel. [As] the wheel is like a great mirror, for [the di]scrimination of all things [... is] in it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Concluding substrate summary. The mirror analogy maps wheel→mirror for cosmic discrimination — both sides stay in the cosmic system. 'Discrimination of all things' refers to the wheel's capacity to differentiate cosmic states, not to a moral or institutional application. The chapter closes without any exhortation or institutional extension — unusual purity.
